the empirical signal separation (ESS) algorithm is an effective tool for separating non-stationary multicomponent signals, which is more powerful than EMD and its ensemble versions.
the proposed method is a powerful signal reconstruction tool.
the new method is able to extract the signal components from non stationary multicomponents signals with fast varying frequencies, which the EMD and ensemble EMD may not.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new signal separation method for non stationary signals.
the development of a new signal reconstruction algorithm for the separation of multicomponent signals, which can be used for the non stationary signal separation.

the following issues: (i) how to utilize the advantages of the empirical mode decomposition and the linear time frequency analysis to separate multicomponent signals, (ii) how to separate multicomponents with fast varying frequency.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed algorithm is a powerful tool to separate multicomponent signals and to extract instantaneous frequencies of the components.

the proposed empirical signal separation algorithm (ESSA) has better performance in separating non stationary multicomponents signal with fast varying frequency than the standard EMD, the ensemble EMD and the synchrosqueeze transform.
, the proposed method is more effective in separating the non-stationary signal than the standard EMD and ensemble EMD.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed method has the advantages of EEMD and STFT or WT in signal reconstruction.
the proposed method can be used to separate non stationary multichannel multicomponent signals.

the proposed method can extract the components in TF plane adaptively, automatically and efficiently, and the extracted TF components can be used to reconstruct the original signal with a higher signal to noise ratio than the other three methods.
